biography:
The Womack Sisters are a Los Angeles-based retro soul and R&B vocal trio made up of sisters BG, Zeimani, and Kucha Womack. They come from one of American music’s most storied families: they are the granddaughters of Sam Cooke, the daughters of Cecil and Linda Womack of Womack & Womack, and the nieces of Bobby Womack.

Raised around music while living in places including London, Amsterdam, Thailand, Kenya, and the Bahamas, the sisters sang from a young age and performed as background vocalists for their parents and uncle before stepping out on their own. They introduced themselves as a trio with self-released singles such as “Darling” and later built momentum with releases including the 2022 EP Legacy, which blended contemporary R&B with a classic soul feel.

Their sound is rooted in rich harmonies, gospel-inflected emotion, and a throwback aesthetic that recalls girl-group and early soul traditions while still feeling current. After signing with Daptone Records, they continued that approach with music designed to honor their family legacy while establishing their own voice in modern retro soul.
name: The Womack Sisters

lastfm.bio_content: Kucha, Zeimani, and BG were singing before they could walk. They grew up on stages and in studios all over the world, singing behind their parents as well as their Uncle Bob. No matter where they called home—London, Thailand, Amsterdam, Kenya, West Virginia, the Bahamas—music and family were always a constant at the center of their lives. As they grew up, each with their own journeys and heartaches, they found their own voices and their own way. Kucha, the youngest of the three, has a pure soulful tone, with a gritty sweetness that betrays her Curtis and Smokey influences. Zeimani’s voice is rich, full, and sultry, laced in rhythm and able to creep from a moan to a squall with silky smoothness. The power and range of BG’s voice seems boundless. She has her grandfather’s uncanny ability to move between the cleanest pop runs and the bluesiest gospel growls without compromising either. As a trio, their three distinct voices become one instrument, playfully trading leads and blossoming into perfectly blended harmonies as only sisters can. In 2016, a mutual friend introduced the Sisters to Daptone co-owner and producer Gabriel Roth (Bosco Mann,) who heard them sing and fell quickly and deeply in love with their voices. Soon after, they met up at Daptone’s Penrose Studios in Riverside, California to cut their first 45 together, “If You Want Me” b/w “I Just Don’t Want You (To Say Goodbye).” Read more on Last.fm.
